vignette: A 66-year-old man with hypertension has sudden vertigo and vomiting and cannot stand. Head impulse testing is normal, there is direction-changing nystagmus, and there is no weakness, hearing loss or facial numbness.
stem: Which arterial territory is most likely involved?

options.text: Medial branch of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (nodulus and uvula)

explanation: Acute vertigo with a normal head impulse test, direction-changing nystagmus and inability to stand is a central vestibular lesion, most often a medial PICA infarct of the nodulus and uvula (lobules IX-X); AICA infarcts add deafness and facial weakness, and lateral medullary involvement adds crossed sensory loss.
